newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police say gathering information on Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Japan police say gathering information on Nomura.

text.p: The Japanese police are gathering information on a case where two Nomura Securities Co Ltd directors made apparently illegal deals, a national police official said on Friday.

"The police have been gathering information and are continuing to do so. Since the SESC (Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission) is investigating the case, we will cooperate with them," an official of the National Policy Agency told a key parliamentary committee.

The scandal broke last week when Nomura said two of its directors, who subsequently resigned, had made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client linked by Japanese media to a former "sokaiya" racketeer.
Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki resigned from his post on Friday to atone for the scandal.

Shozo Wakabayashi, secretary-general of the executive bureau of the SESC, also told the same parliamentary committee that the securities watchdog was continuing to conduct an investigation into the Nomura incident.

Asked about reports that the other "Big Four" brokerages have had links with the sokaiya racketeer, Wakabayashi said: "I am aware of various media reports, but I would like to refrain from commenting on them."

The Mainichi Shimbun newspaper reported on Friday that the SESC found that the corporate clients linked to the sokaiya racketeer opened accounts with Daiwa Securities Co Ltd , Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd at the same time as they did so at Nomura.
The SESC has been investigating the three brokerages' transactions with the client, the paper said.
